outline: 1013 Angles in a Right Angle and Straight Line

examples.solution_text:
Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so $a=64^{\circ}$.
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}x+64^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\x&=180^{\circ}-64^{\circ}\\x&=116^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $a=57^{\circ}$.
Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal, so $x=a=57^{\circ}$.

Corresponding angles on parallel lines are equal, so $a=112^{\circ}$.
Co-interior angles between parallel lines add to $180^{\circ}$.
$\begin{aligned}x+112^{\circ}&=180^{\circ}\\x&=180^{\circ}-112^{\circ}\\x&=68^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Corresponding angles give a=64°. The adjacent straight-line angle is x=180°−64°=116°. The marked sectors agree with these relationships.
The angle vertically opposite 57° is a=57°. The marked lower angle x is alternate to a, so x=57°.
Corresponding angles give a=112°. The marked x and a are co-interior, so x=180°−112°=68°. The transversal's 68° inclination agrees with the marked sectors.
Alternate angles transfer 43° and 72° to the lower line at P. Thus 43°+x+72°=180°, giving x=65°. The rays at P have directions 137° and 72°, independently confirming the 65° sector.

Constructing the parallel through P transfers 32° and 46° by alternate angles. They are adjacent parts of the marked smaller angle, so x=32°+46°=78°. The solid rays have directions 32° and −46°, confirming 78°.
